Eleven case studies — Wise, Duolingo, Jaguar, Cracker Barrel, Coinbase, Sky, Nubank, Stripe, Ramp, Liquid Death, Oatly
A working strategy for cap.app — private credit, made legible

body.x: The magazine is built in five movements. Part one is the theory — nine chapters on what marketing actually is, positioning, category, jobs to be done, awareness stages, mental availability, and the specific cognitive failure that afflicts every technical founder alive. Part two is the craft: how sentences get made, how hard ideas get explained, how proof gets constructed, how pages get built.

Part three is eleven case studies, weighted to the last two years, each one chosen because it teaches something you will need in the Cap room. Part four is the engagement itself — a full diagnosis of Cap's current communication, a five-audience map, three positioning candidates, a message hierarchy, rewritten copy for every section of the homepage, a campaign architecture, a measurement plan, a ninety-day sequence, and a commercial structure you can put in front of him. Part five is the toolkit: the fifty marketing instruments sitting on your machine right now, what each one does, and which to reach for when.

Cap is not a company with a bad website. Cap is a company whose product is genuinely, structurally difficult — three-sided, novel, and operating in two domains (private credit and crypto) that each carry their own suspicion. The temptation with a client like this is to make the words shorter and call it a day. Shorter words on an unsorted idea produce a shorter unsorted idea.

The actual work is upstream of the words: decide who you are for, decide what you are on the shelf beside, decide what single thing you want lodged in a stranger's head, and only then write. Benjamin has been told to use fewer words. Nobody has told him which words to keep. That is the job.

body.x: Everything a strategist needs to know before opening their mouth in the first meeting.

Cap is a credit platform built on Ethereum. Depositors put in dollar-stable assets and receive cUSD, which can be staked into stcUSD to earn yield. That yield is generated by lending the reserves to whitelisted institutional borrowers. What makes the structure unusual is the third side: underwriters escrow their own capital behind each borrower, so that if a borrower defaults, the underwriter's collateral is liquidated to make the depositor whole.1

The company's own one-line description, from its About page, is: “Cap is a covered credit application consisting of a digital dollar, a credit platform, and a financial guarantee market to underwrite individual loans.”2 Note that this sentence contains four nouns a layman does not hold: covered credit, digital dollar, credit platform, financial guarantee market. It is accurate. It is also, for most readers, four unknowns in a row.

Traditional private credit has a principal–agent problem: the people who decide which loans to make do not personally lose money when those loans go bad.3 Cap's design forces the decision-maker to post collateral. In the founder's words to Yahoo Finance: “The people that make decisions over allocating capital at Cap are tied directly to the loss.”4 That is the whole idea. Everything else is implementation.

body.x: Marketing is not promotion after the product is finished. It is the discipline that decides who the product is for, what value it creates, how that value is framed, and how exchange happens.

The American Marketing Association defines marketing around creating, communicating, delivering and exchanging offerings of value. The useful word is not communicating. It is value. A company can post every day and still avoid the marketing problem if it has not decided which value matters to which market.

Four kinds of work are commonly collapsed into one word: market strategy chooses where to play; product marketing supplies the market context; brand builds memory and meaning; promotion buys or earns attention. A fifth function—sales—converts specific opportunities. They cooperate, but they are not substitutes.

Once you know how a system works, it becomes difficult to imagine what it is like not to know. Technical accuracy can therefore increase while communication quality declines.

Experts compress knowledge into terms that carry entire systems for them. A novice receives only the term. When Cap says covered credit, financial guarantee market, shared security network or utilisation curve, the team sees mechanisms; a newcomer sees four locked doors.

Brand creates future preference and memory; demand activity converts present intent. Early-stage marketing needs both, but the split should follow the company's market, sales cycle and evidence—not a universal ratio.

Brand and performance are often framed as rivals because their effects appear on different clocks. Demand capture can show a click today. Brand can change the probability of recognition, trust and selection months before the buyer enters a measurable funnel.
